rich_summary: Arjuna finally confronts Karna on the battlefield. After noticing Karna’s bowstring twang, Arjuna abandons his clash with Aswatthaman and rushes to face his long‑time rival. The two exchange bitter taunts: Arjuna recalls Karna’s boastfulness and his silent complicity during Draupadi’s humiliation, vowing that the exile and suffering of the Pandavas will now be avenged. Karna responds with scorn, questioning Arjuna’s past restraint and challenging him to prove his strength in deeds. Their duel erupts in a fierce storm of arrows. Arjuna gradually gains the advantage—cutting Karna’s bow, killing his horses, and finally striking him with a powerful arrow that pierces his armor and leaves him reeling, forcing Karna to flee. Afterward, Arjuna asks to face Bhishma, while his charioteer Uttara confesses terror at the overwhelming violence of the battle.

highlight_spans.why: Sets the stage for the long‑awaited confrontation as Arjuna notices Karna and turns from other foes to face him.
Arjuna’s opening challenge to Karna, calling him to justify the boasts he once made in the Kuru assembly.
Arjuna invokes the humiliation of Draupadi, tying the duel to the moral outrage that fuels the Pandavas’ vengeance.
Turning point of the duel where Arjuna destroys Karna’s advantage and strikes a devastating arrow through his armor.
Uttara’s vivid description of terror and sensory overload captures the overwhelming horror of the battlefield.

top_scenes.scene_text: Arjuna and Karna facing each other in chariots amid a storm of arrows, both drawing their bows as the battlefield roars around them.
Arjuna’s blazing arrow piercing Karna’s armored chest as Karna reels in his chariot and his horses collapse beneath him.
Uttara gripping the reins in panic while Arjuna stands calm with the Gandiva glowing like a ring of fire amid smoke, blood, and shattered chariots.
